messages:
neha: Heads up — after pushing CUDA 12.3 + driver 545 to us-west1-gpu, a handful of nodes report MIG profiles gone and pods in CrashLoopBackOff. Seeing weird UUIDs.
matt: which nodes? any common kernel/driver diffs?
sasha: node list pls + `nvidia-smi` output if available.
neha: nodes: gpu-node-23, gpu-node-27, gpu-node-31. grabbed quick outputs:
```
$ ssh gpu-node-23 sudo nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (UUID: GPU-709d8a1f-...)
GPU 1: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (UUID: GPU-7f23b9c2-...)

$ sudo nvidia-smi mig -lgci
No MIG instances found on device 0
No MIG instances found on device 1
```
But kube shows pods bound to MIG profiles that used to exist (1g.5gb etc).
```
kubectl describe pod ml-worker-5 -n inference
  Warning  FailedScheduling  ...  no matching device plugin objects
```
matt: hmm — seems like persistent MIG config didn't survive driver module reload. Did the upgrade flip `nvidia-persistenced` or the MIG partitioning tool version?
neha: driver package replaced kernel module and we tested on canary only for 24h. there was an automated `apt` kernel patch too on some nodes.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: CUDA 12.3 driver-545 rollout completed at 2026-03-18T09:12Z to us-west1-gpu batch-17
sasha: any sign of UUID drift? earlier we've seen device index <-> UUID remap after module reloads.
neha: yes — comparing `/var/lib/nvidia/gpu-uuid.map` before/after (we have backups) — mapping changed for gpu-node-27. some entries show GPU-709d8a1f -> GPU-4cbb... (different UUID)
oliver: if device UUIDs changed, the MIG device plugin (and our node-local mapping) will mismatch the stored profile IDs. That explains pods referencing old UUIDs.
jen: can we recreate MIG profiles in place? risk losing running state.
sasha: agree — plan: cordon problematic nodes, drain non-stateful pods, reapply MIG profiles (via `nvidia-smi mig -cci` / mig-config tool), restart device plugin, uncordon. For stateful inference pods, fallback to other nodes.
neha: attempted on gpu-node-23 quickly:
```
sudo nvidia-smi mig -c -i 0 -g 1g.5gb
Error: MIG partitioning disabled: device in compute mode
```
matt: compute mode blocks partitioning — need to set persistence + disable compute mode temporarily. We should schedule drain window.
oncall: running an emergency rolling window now. I'm going to cordon gpu-node-23/27/31 and move eligible pods. ETA ~30m.
infra-bot: cluster-autoscaler: scale events suppressed while nodes cordoned in us-west1-gpu
neha: after draining, I reconfigured MIG on gpu-node-23 and re-created the 1g profiles, restarted device plugin — kube now sees devices but UUIDs on MIG instances differ from pre-upgrade. Some pods still referencing old instance UUIDs so they failed to bind.
oliver: that's expected — MIG instance UUIDs are ephemeral on re-create. Device plugin should register new MIG instance IDs; pods with device allocations from the kubelet will need eviction + reschedule to pick up new ones.
sasha: so remediation steps:
  1) cordon node
  2) drain non-stateful pods
  3) ensure `nvidia-persistenced` + compute mode adjustments
  4) reapply MIG partitions with mig-config version X (match pre-upgrade if possible)
  5) restart GPU device plugin and wait for `kubelet` to register new device resources
  6) uncordon and let pods re-schedule
jen: for stateful pipelines, we should migrate traffic first. also consider rolling driver rollback for remaining nodes if root cause is driver->kernel mismatch.
matt: besides UUIDs, we also saw NCCL errors in logs for distributed trainers — maybe ABI mismatch between 545 driver and NCCL 2.18 pinned in our runtime. Need to watch for performance regressions.
oncall: actioned: cordoned cluster nodes and started draining. I'll post progress.
neha: quick patch worked for gpu-node-23/31 — reapply + restart gave green, but gpu-node-27 needed rollback to driver 535 because its kernel package was different and `nvidia.ko` failed to load the MIG ops.
oliver: follow-up: add preflight job in canary rollout that verifies:
  - `nvidia-smi mig -lgci` preserves expected profile counts
  - GPU UUIDs mapping stable across module reload
  - device-plugin registers expected resource names
sasha: also add an automated snapshot of `/var/lib/nvidia` and the mig config pre-upgrade, to allow quick restore.
jen: logging follow-up ticket and patch for rollout docs.
neha: thanks — marking nodes recovered: gpu-node-23 ✅ gpu-node-31 ✅ gpu-node-27 rolled back and will be re-run in a smaller window. we'll keep small canary with kernel+driver pinned.
matt: +1. also let's add a note to the runbook about compute mode requirement and MIG ephemeral UUIDs.
oncall: closing loop here — removing cordon after validation. Will escalate if more drift shows up. :white_check_mark:
